analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: Framing Off Balance Sheet Liabilities in the AI Ecosystem
key_insights: Market participants increasingly view AI-related issuers' capital structures holistically, and GS says access to debt financing is a strategic competitive advantage.

Hyperscaler free cash flow has turned negative and debt issuance has accelerated. More than $40B of deals were announced since October 29, and hyperscalers have issued $271B of debt year to date, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250B.
Part of the 2026 issuance reflects a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply. GS sees scope for more, with market access uneven across issuers and dependent on market tone.
GS estimates $657B of year-to-date global AI-related debt issuance across syndicated credit markets through November 2, which is far larger than the five hyperscalers alone.
GS tracks $1.7T of hyperscaler lease commitments, 75% of which have not yet commenced, and estimates $1.9T of aggregate unconditional purchase commitments, $685B of which is due by year-end 2027.

GS says part of the off-balance-sheet amount is captured in consensus capex forecasts, but this fast-growing category is still an additional use of cash. It supports GS's view that debt financing across syndicated and private markets will play a key role in the AI buildout.

Faster near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less debt issuance. Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments are the key risks to more issuance, subject to market conditions.

Rating agencies treat off-balance-sheet liabilities differently, with S&P more conservative. Since early August their posture has become more cautious, with some lowered outlooks and commentary about little margin for error. GS says evidence of monetization by 2028 is key to limiting downward pressure on ratings.
risk_factors: Delayed monetization of AI investment and growth in purchase commitments could drive more debt issuance, subject to market conditions.
Capital markets access may be uneven across issuers and depends heavily on market tone.
Rating agencies have lowered some outlooks and cite little margin for error, so downward pressure on AI ecosystem ratings is possible without evidence of monetization by 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: Faster near-term monetization of AI investment would reduce the need for debt issuance, so less debt issuance is the outcome in that case.
tension_points.bear_case: Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments would drive more debt issuance, subject to market conditions. Rating agencies have also turned more cautious, citing little margin for error.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of AI monetization by 2028, which GS says is key to mitigating downward pressure on debt ratings.
